contents.name: §2.3.2 Positive Linear Functionals
contents.reason: This section develops order-cone positivity and positive extensions; this pair uses unrestricted normed-space functionals and introduces no ordered vector-space structure.

contents.name: Definition 2.37 (Ordered Vector Space)
contents.reason: Its cone axioms belong only to the omitted positive-functional theory and do not enter the gauge, separation, annihilator, or complement arguments.

contents.name: Theorem 2.38 (Hahn--Banach for Positive Linear Functionals)
contents.reason: Positive domination by an ordered cone is a different extension theorem from the analytic Hahn--Banach prerequisite used in this geometric development.

contents.name: Exercise 2.39 (direct Zorn proof of Theorem 2.38)
contents.reason: It is a second proof route for the excluded positive-extension theorem rather than a lemma needed by the selected geometric route.

contents.name: Exercise 2.40 (failure of positive extension without O3)
contents.reason: The counterexample concerns an order-theoretic axiom for positive functionals on continuous functions, absent from this normed-space separation page.

contents.name: Exercise 2.42 (nonempty-interior hypothesis cannot be omitted)
contents.reason: Its empty-interior ell-squared sets share a closure; the companion gives the directly relevant elementary zero-distance obstruction to strong separation.

contents.name: Exercise 2.43 (dense difference of two closed convex ell-squared sets)
contents.reason: This stronger infinite-dimensional construction has no affine separator and requires its separate exercise proof; it is not needed to state the compactness hypothesis sharply.

contents.name: Lemma 2.44 (interior and closure of a convex set)
Lemma 2.45 (strict inequality on an interior passes to the closure)
Exercise 2.47 (affine hyperplanes as inverse images under nonzero bounded functionals)
Corollary 2.48 (open convex set disjoint from a subspace)
Corollary 2.49 (open convex set as intersection of open half-spaces)
Corollary 2.50 (strong separation of closed and compact convex sets)
Exercise 2.51 (a closed convex set is an intersection of closed half-spaces)
Theorem 2.53 (Hahn--Banach for a subspace and an exterior point)
Corollary 2.57 (duals of subspaces and quotient spaces)
contents.reason: The restriction and quotient-dual identifications require full dual-space and quotient-factorisation machinery, whose planned home treats these maps and their norms together.

contents.name: Corollary 2.58 (quotient-dual norm identities)
contents.reason: These exact norm equalities follow from the deferred restriction and quotient-dual identification, so they belong where those maps are formally defined.

contents.name: Exercise 2.60 (equivalent complement, projection, and right-inverse formulations)
Statement after Lemma 2.61 (Phillips: c-zero is not complemented in ell-infinity)

contents.reason: This example treats failure of separation when neither set supplies the required openness; the companion instead gives a closed-set zero-distance example tailored to strong separation.

contents.name: Corollary 5.4 (closed convex and compact sets are strongly separated)
Corollary 5.5 (open convex set and a subspace)
Problem 5.3 (polar and prepolar)
contents.reason: Polars need the dual pairing and a separate polar calculus, so they belong with adjoints and annihilators rather than this first separation treatment.

contents.name: Problem 5.4 (bipolar theorem)
contents.reason: The bipolar theorem is a global locally convex duality result; this pair supplies only the continuous-functional separation needed before weak topologies are built.

contents.name: Weak-star topology sigma(X*,X)
contents.reason: Weak-star neighbourhoods and their comparison with weak neighbourhoods need the full dual pairing and are deferred to the dedicated topology page.

contents.name: Theorem 5.10 (Banach--Alaoglu)
contents.reason: Weak-star compactness of the dual ball uses a product compactness construction absent from this local separation page and has a dedicated later home.

contents.name: Example after Theorem 5.11 (weak closure of the unit sphere)
contents.reason: The unit-sphere weak-closure phenomenon needs finite-codimensional weak neighbourhoods and is best developed once the weak topology is available.

contents.name: Theorem 5.13 (Goldstine)
contents.reason: Goldstine concerns weak-star density of the primal unit ball in the bidual, requiring bidual notation and weak-star topology beyond this pair.
